units.title: Forecast: gales easing, clearing later
units.author: met
units.text: Marrow Sound, issued 06:00 ST. The yellow wind warning remains in force until 12:00. Westerly gale 8 at first, gusting 55 knots on exposed headlands, decreasing 6 by afternoon. Heavy showers this morning, dying out from the west after midday. Sea state rough, becoming moderate. Visibility good except in showers. Maximum 9 C. Tonight: mainly clear, wind light, a slight frost possible inland around Brackwater.

units.title: Service update: storm disruption
units.author: ferry
units.text: Sound Lines. The 07:10 Port Ammet to Lisle and Gilliver sailing is cancelled due to sea conditions at the Lisle approach. The 09:30 sailing will operate subject to a weather check at 08:45. Passengers with vehicles booked on cancelled sailings will be transferred automatically. Please do not travel to the terminal without checking this page first. We apologise for the continued disruption.

units.title: Storm restoration: progress
units.author: power
units.text: Sound Power Co-op. Overnight crews restored supply to 1,140 properties in the Tollinby and Brackwater areas. Around 210 properties remain off, mainly on the Brackwater ridge road where two poles are down across the lane. A generator has been placed at the Brackwater village hall, which is open as a warm space from 09:00. We expect most remaining customers back by this evening. Please treat any fallen line as live.

units.title: Roads: storm closures
units.author: council
units.text: Ammet District Council. The following roads remain closed because of fallen trees: the Brackwater ridge road between the reservoir car park and Holly Lane; the lower Tollinby road at the Mill Bridge, where the verge has slipped. The Gilliver harbour road is open but reduced to one lane at the sea wall. Our crews are prioritising bus routes and school routes. Report blocked drains through the usual form, not by phoning the depot.

units.title: Week three: quick check-in
units.author: ruth_imber
units.text: Hi, glad to see the worst of the weather has gone through. A few things: the supply boat charter is not affected by the Sound Lines changes, it's a separate operator. The Met Office says light winds tomorrow, so it should be a full day. Just checking where we are on numbers when you have a moment; head office like a figure for the Thursday meeting. Thanks, Ruth

units.title: Day-rate register updated (ref GLS-DR-0416)
units.author: grieve_payroll
units.text: This is an automated message. The day-rate register for contract KH-30 has been updated with attendance to the end of the previous working day. Status: RECORDED. No action is required unless the figures differ from your site log. Queries should be raised with Operations, not by replying to this address. This mailbox is not monitored.

units.title: Your updated policy documents are ready
units.author: lyle_insurance
units.text: Good morning from Lyle Mutual. Following your recent renewal, your updated vehicle policy schedule (ref LM-V-55102) is now available in your online account. Nothing in your cover has changed, but please read the schedule and keep it somewhere safe. Peace of mind starts with knowing what you're covered for. Small print: documents remain available for six years.

units.title: After the storm: dry kit, warm camp!
units.author: camp_supply_news
units.text: Hello from Camp Supply! Rough few days out there? Our after-the-storm bundle is back: tarp clips, a peg mallet, two rolls of seam tape and a drying line, all for less than the price of a takeaway. Plus five ways to dry boots without cooking them (tip three: newspaper, changed twice). Stay warm, stay dry, and remember our lanterns are the brightest in the Sound!

units.title: Storm blows itself out after three days of gales
units.author: courier
units.text: The storm that has battered the Marrow Sound since the start of the week was easing by mid-morning, leaving fallen trees, a slipped verge at Tollinby and a long list of jobs for council and power crews. Forecasters expect the wind to drop to a light breeze by evening, with clear skies and a frost inland overnight.

units.author: courier
units.text: At its height, a gust of 61 knots was recorded at Carrow Point. In Gilliver, waves topped the sea wall on two high tides, and the harbour road was reduced to one lane after stones were thrown up onto the carriageway. Harbour users spent yesterday doubling mooring lines; one small rowing boat was lost from the inner harbour and has not been found.

units.author: courier
units.text: Sound Power Co-op said around 1,350 properties lost supply at some point during the storm, most of them in the Brackwater and Tollinby areas, where trees brought down lines. By this morning all but about 200 had been reconnected. The co-op thanked customers for their patience and asked people not to approach fallen lines, however dead they look.

units.author: courier
units.text: Ferry services were badly disrupted, with several sailings cancelled on each day of the storm. Sound Lines said the morning service would run once the Lisle approach was checked. The company separately confirmed changes to its night timetable, which are reported elsewhere in this edition.

units.author: courier
units.text: There were no reports of serious injury. Port Ammet General said it had treated a handful of people for cuts and sprains, including a man who was blown off his feet outside the market hall while carrying a sheet of plywood. 'He was trying to board up his shop window,' a relative said. 'The plywood won.'

units.title: Sound Lines cuts night crossings for 'crew welfare review'
units.author: courier
units.text: Sound Lines is to reduce its night crossings between Port Ammet, Lisle and Gilliver from this week while it carries out what the company calls a crew welfare review. The last evening sailing from Port Ammet will leave at 20:15 instead of 23:40, and the late return from Gilliver will not run until further notice.

units.author: courier
units.text: In a short statement, the operator said it was 'reviewing rostering, rest periods and support for crew working night services' and that the change was temporary. It did not say how long the review would take or what had prompted it. Asked whether it was connected to recent reports of trespass on the Gilliver and Lisle slipways, a spokesperson said the company 'does not comment on individual staff matters'.

units.author: courier
units.text: Earlier this month the Gilliver harbourmaster issued a notice reminding the public that slipways are working areas and must not be used for fishing or loitering after dark, after crew on two separate nights reported a person standing at the water's edge who did not respond to a hail.

units.author: courier
units.text: Commuters from Lisle said the change would hit shift workers hardest. 'If you finish at ten at the hospital, you now have nowhere to sleep but your car,' said one, who asked not to be named. The council said it would ask the operator whether a bus link to the Gilliver road could be arranged in the meantime.

units.author: courier
units.text: Freight and the separate supply charters that serve outlying moorings are not affected. The seafarers' branch that represents Sound Lines deck crew said it had been consulted and supported 'any review that puts people first', but would be watching to make sure the reduced timetable did not quietly become permanent.

units.title: Live: storm clean-up across the Sound
units.author: soundfm
units.text: 07:40. Good morning. The wind is finally dropping at Port Ammet, though it is still blowing hard at the Lisle approach and the first ferry is off. We'll be keeping this page updated through the morning with roads, power and schools. Send us your pictures of the damage, but please don't stand under anything to take them.

units.author: soundfm
units.text: 08:15. Schools: Tollinby Primary and the Lisle school are open as normal. Brackwater Primary opens at 10:00 because the ridge road is still shut and two staff can't get in. The secondary school bus from Gilliver is running about twenty minutes late because of the single-lane section at the sea wall.

units.author: soundfm
units.text: 09:05. A listener in Tollinby sends a picture of a garden shed that has travelled two gardens down and landed upright, door still shut. She says the lawnmower is still inside. Elsewhere, a large beech is down across the lower Tollinby road near the Mill Bridge, and the verge beside it has slipped into the beck.

units.author: soundfm
units.text: 10:00. Sound Lines says the 09:30 sailing did go, about forty minutes late. The skipper reported a heavy swell at Lisle but nothing dangerous. The operator has also confirmed reduced night crossings from this week; we're asking them for more detail and will bring it to you when we have it.

units.author: soundfm
units.text: 11:30. Power: the co-op says around 200 homes are still without electricity, almost all on the Brackwater ridge. The village hall there has a generator, hot drinks and phone charging. Volunteers say they could use more flasks, and a second kettle would be appreciated.

units.author: soundfm
units.text: 13:10. The Met Office has cancelled the wind warning an hour early. Blue sky over Carrow Point for the first time in three days. We're closing this page now. Thanks to everyone who sent pictures, especially of the travelling shed, which has become something of a newsroom favourite.

units.author: met
units.text: Warning update, 11:00 ST. The yellow wind warning for the Marrow Sound has been cancelled. Winds are now westerly 5 to 6 and continuing to ease. Showers have cleared from the west. A small-craft advisory remains in place until 18:00 for a lingering heavy swell off Carrow Point and in the Lisle approach.

units.title: Notice to mariners: storm debris
units.author: coast
units.text: Coastguard, Marrow Sound. Mariners are advised of floating debris following the recent storm, including timber, fish boxes and a partly submerged wooden rowing boat reported adrift south of Gilliver harbour. Keep a good lookout, particularly in the channel between Gilliver and Kittering Holm. Report sightings of significant debris on channel 16.

units.author: coast
units.text: Coastguard, Marrow Sound. The east cardinal buoy marking the Lisle Spit is reported dragged approximately 80 metres off its charted position and its light is unreliable. Vessels should give the spit a wide berth until the buoy has been re-laid by the tender, expected within three days, weather permitting.

units.title: Night timetable change
units.author: ferry
units.text: Sound Lines. From tonight, and until further notice, night crossings are reduced while we carry out a crew welfare review. The last sailing from Port Ammet to Lisle and Gilliver departs at 20:15. The 23:40 departure and the 00:55 return from Gilliver will not operate. Daytime sailings are unchanged. We are sorry for the inconvenience and thank customers for their understanding.

units.title: Recycling collections resume
units.author: council
units.text: Ammet District Council. The Port Ammet blue-bin recycling round will run today on its normal route, including Rope Walk, Market Row and the Quay streets, following the vehicle repair that disrupted recent collections. If your bin was not emptied in the last three weeks, extra bags of clean recycling placed beside it will be taken today only.

units.author: power
units.text: Sound Power Co-op, 16:30. Supply has been restored to the Brackwater ridge road after crews replaced two poles and re-strung about 300 metres of line. Fewer than 20 properties remain off on individual faults; engineers will visit each one this evening. The Brackwater warm space will close at 18:00. Thank you for your patience.

units.author: met
units.text: Evening forecast, 18:00 ST. Clear and calm overnight, wind variable 2 or less. Minimum 1 C on the coast, minus 2 C around Brackwater, with patchy frost on untreated roads. Some mist may form over the reservoir and in sheltered inlets near dawn. Tomorrow: dry, sunny spells, light winds. High water at Gilliver 04:52 and 17:18.

units.title: Dellow Court tenants ask for a date on stairwell lights
units.author: weypost
units.text: Residents of Dellow Court have asked the building's managing agent for a firm date to repair the stairwell lighting between the sixth and eighth floors, which they say has been failing for more than two weeks. The 14-storey block, owned by Kerrow Estates, houses around 160 households.

units.author: weypost
units.text: Kerrow Estates has said in notices to tenants that the fault lies with a timer relay on the riser serving those floors and that a replacement part has been ordered. Residents say the notices have repeated that message several times without giving a date. 'We are told to be patient,' said the secretary of the residents' association. 'We are very patient. We would also like light.'

units.author: weypost
units.text: Older residents and parents with pushchairs are the worst affected when the lift is out of service, which tenants say has happened twice this month. Some have taken to carrying torches. The corner shop on the ground floor says it has sold more torches in a fortnight than in the previous year.

units.author: weypost
units.text: The Post has seen online discussion among residents about noises in the stairwell at night, which some attribute to plant equipment and others to people using the stairs. Kerrow Estates said it had 'no evidence of unauthorised access' and would 'continue to keep residents informed'.

units.title: Holm clearance enters second half with client still silent
units.author: tradejournal
units.text: Grieve Land Services' 30-day clearance of Kittering Holm, the largest single-site vegetation contract let in the Marrow Sound for a decade, has passed its midpoint. The firm has not published progress figures and declined to comment beyond confirming that work is 'continuing to programme' after this week's storm.

units.author: tradejournal
units.text: Industry observers have questioned the economics of the job. At a reported $100 a tree plus day rates, the contract is generous by regional standards, but a small crew working a forested island with no road access faces high costs in fuel, transport and lost days. 'Somebody wants it done fast and doesn't mind paying for it,' one contractor told the Journal.

units.author: tradejournal
units.text: The owner, Ardent Vale Holdings, has made no statement about its plans for the cleared land. Its planning application describes only 'total vegetation clearance' with standard conditions on run-off and nesting birds. There is no application for buildings or access works on record.

units.author: tradejournal
units.text: Timber from the Holm is expected to be sold as mixed softwood once the logs are brought off. Merchants in Port Ammet say prices for mixed softwood have softened slightly this month, partly because storm-felled timber from inland estates is coming onto the market at the same time.

units.title: Recycling lorry back on the road after three missed weeks
units.author: courier
units.text: Blue bins in central Port Ammet were finally emptied today after the council's recycling round was suspended for three weeks while its only spare lorry waited for a replacement gearbox. Residents in Rope Walk and Market Row had complained of overflowing bins and gulls.

units.author: courier
units.text: The council said it had underestimated how long the part would take to arrive and apologised for not communicating the delay more clearly. Councillors on the environment committee have asked for a report on why the district has only one spare vehicle for a round that serves more than 9,000 homes.

units.author: courier
units.text: One Rope Walk resident, a retired postman who said he had written to the council every week of the delay, described the return of the lorry as 'a small victory for the ratepayer' and said he would be checking that the crew put the lids back on properly.

units.title: Harbourmaster repeats slipway safety plea
units.author: soundfm
units.text: Gilliver's harbourmaster has repeated her request for people to stay off the village slipway after dark, saying storm damage has left loose stones and weed on the lower section. Her notice quotes the harbour byelaw on working areas and asks parents to remind teenagers that the slipway is not a place to hang about.

units.author: soundfm
units.text: Asked by Sound FM whether the notice was connected to the change in night ferry crossings, the harbourmaster said she could not comment on Sound Lines' staffing and that the slipway notice 'is about slipways'. The harbour office is open weekdays from 08:00 for anyone who wants to report damage.

units.title: Brackwater reservoir near full after storm rain
units.author: soundfm
units.text: The Brackwater reservoir is at 97 per cent of capacity after three days of heavy rain, and the water authority says the overflow channel may run for the first time this autumn. Walkers are asked to keep away from the spillway and the outflow pipe at the dam foot, where the ground is soft.

units.author: soundfm
units.text: The reservoir car park will stay open, but the estate's ranger says the woodland paths below the dam are flooded in places and closed to the public after dusk until further notice. 'They should be closed after dusk anyway,' he told us. 'People keep wandering about in there at night.'

units.title: Supply boat: revised times this week
units.author: ruth_imber
units.text:
Hi, the charter skipper has asked to move the next run to a morning slot. So:
- next boat leaves Gilliver 07:40, alongside the Holm landing about 08:10
- deck cargo as normal; fuel in the usual drums
- if anything urgent is missing from the list, I need it by 14:00 tomorrow
He says he'd rather not be on the water in the evenings this week, which is his call. Thanks, Ruth

units.author: ruth_imber
units.text: One more thing, sorry. Payroll have flagged that the crew balance is showing outstanding on the register. I know it's hard to get to the terminal in weather like this week's, but if it can be settled before the weekend run that would stop head office asking me about it. People notice these things on a job this remote. Thanks, Ruth

units.title: what do you call a tree that fits in your hand
units.author: hal_brannock
units.text: a palm. you're welcome chief. road job here is all mud and a foreman who thinks a chainsaw is a personality. anyway. I've been reading the Courier stuff. Grieve has done jobs like this before. Ask about the Corran job. Ask Ruth if you like, see what her face does down the phone. right, tea's ready. H

units.author: hal_brannock
units.text: re my last. I'm not going to write it down, chief, so don't ask. it was years ago and I wasn't even on the island side of it, I was on the boats. just ask. and keep your lot together of an evening, that's free advice from someone who's been a site lead longer than you've had a beard. H

units.title: Mum's date + the dog has opinions
units.author: sam
units.text: hiya, so the hospital rang and Mum's hip is the day after tomorrow, first on the list, which she's thrilled about because it means no breakfast and she can complain about it. I'm taking her in at seven. she says don't ring, you're busy, which means ring. anyway the dog chewed the remote, only the volume button, so now the telly is either silent or deafening. the play is next week, Bea is a tree, I'm told it's a speaking tree. love, S x

units.title: Following up: Kittering Holm
units.author: nell_ashdown
units.text:
Hello again. I'm grateful for your patience with my earlier note. Since my piece ran I've had a lot of letters, mostly from Gilliver. Two questions, if you're able:
1. Has the storm affected the camp or the schedule?
2. Has anyone from Ardent Vale visited the site?
I've put the same questions to Grieve and to Ardent Vale. Anything you say can be unattributed. Best wishes, Nell Ashdown

units.title: Sorry, me again
units.author: ana_reyner
units.text: Hello, sorry to write again so soon. I saw the storm on the news and the pictures of the sea wall at Gilliver and I couldn't stop thinking about the tents, or whatever you have out there. I know it's not tents. Is Tomas sleeping? He never sleeps when it's windy, since he was small. Please tell him I'm fine and the cat is fine. Ana

units.title: Courier enquiries
units.author: ruth_imber
units.text: Hi, a reporter from the Courier has rung head office again this afternoon. I've given her the usual line. If she or anyone else contacts you directly, please pass it to me rather than replying, even to say no comment. I'm not suggesting there's anything to hide; it's just simpler if one person speaks for the job. Thanks, Ruth

units.title: A note of thanks from Ardent Vale
units.author: ardentvale_pr
units.text: Dear partner, as the Marrow Sound recovers from this week's weather, we wanted to thank everyone working on our behalf for their resilience. Ardent Vale remains committed to a patient, responsible approach to Kittering Holm and to respecting the Sound and its communities. We have no further plans to announce at this time. Warm regards, Community Information, Ardent Vale

units.title: 1953: 'Light relay for the Holm' (with editor's note)
units.author: courier_archivist
units.text: Editor's note: several readers have asked about a lighthouse relay once planned for Kittering Holm. The paper reported it twice, in the spring of 1953 and the winter of 1954. Both items are reproduced below from page five and page eleven respectively. The paper did not follow the story further, and the archive holds no letters on the subject. G. Faulds, Archive Desk.

units.author: courier_archivist
units.text: Spring 1953, page five: 'The Lights Board has sent a survey party to Kittering Holm to report on the building of a relay station on the island's ridge, which would carry the Carrow Point signal to Lisle and the southern channel. Mr R. Talbot, the Board's engineer, expects the work to take a fortnight. Gilliver boatmen will ferry the party daily.'

units.author: courier_archivist
units.text: Winter 1954, page eleven, in full: 'We understand the proposal for a light relay on Kittering Holm will not proceed. A Board spokesman said the matter had been considered carefully and that other arrangements would serve the channel adequately.' Archive note: no reason was given, and the paper did not ask for one in print. The 'other arrangements' appear to be the Lisle Spit buoys laid in 1955.

units.title: Lights Board survey of Kittering Holm (1953), part 1: purpose and party
units.author: relay_engineer_1950s
units.text: Report to the Lights Board on a proposed relay station, Kittering Holm. 1. Purpose. To determine whether the ridge of the Holm affords a suitable site for an unattended relay light and keeper's hut, extending the Carrow Point signal to the Lisle channel. 2. Party. The undersigned, one assistant surveyor, two chainmen, and a boatman engaged at Gilliver. Fourteen working days on the island, weather permitting.

units.author: relay_engineer_1950s
units.text: 3. Site. The ridge rises to 64 m above datum at its northern knoll. From the knoll Carrow Point light bears 318 degrees, clearly visible; the Lisle pier light bears 201 degrees, visible over the treeline from a 9 m tower. Ground is shallow soil over rock, adequate for footings. Timber cover is dense to the shore on all sides and would require clearance of a strip 40 m wide for the tower and hut.

units.author: relay_engineer_1950s
units.text: 4. Conduct of the survey. Work proceeded normally. It should be recorded that the party asked on the third day to be taken off before dusk each evening rather than camp on the island as planned, and the boatman preferred this also. The additional boat hire is included in the costs below. No time was lost by this arrangement, as work in the trees after dark would not have been practical in any case.

units.title: Kittering Holm relay station (proposed)
units.author: hist_wiki_marsh
units.text: The Kittering Holm relay station was a proposed unattended light on the Holm's northern knoll, surveyed by the Lights Board in 1953 and abandoned in 1954. The society holds a carbon copy of the survey report, donated in 1988 by the family of an assistant surveyor. No construction took place. A concrete survey pillar on the knoll is sometimes taken for a foundation; it is not one. [citation needed: pillar date]

units.author: hist_wiki_pell
units.text: Talk note: the article implies the plan was dropped for mysterious reasons. The report gives its reason plainly: staffing. In 1954 the Board was short of keepers everywhere and was closing stations, not opening them. Buoys were cheaper. I have removed the phrase 'for reasons never explained' from the summary, which was poorly sourced. Pell.

units.title: Holm timber camp diary, J. Penhallow: December entries
units.author: camp_clerk_1894
units.text: Decr 3rd. Wind W, hard frost. Felled 41, the far lines. Paid Trewin and Hosking their week, 9s each. Hosking asks to go across Saturday to his mother, refused, the boat not due. Lamps trimmed at 4 o'clock. Men to their huts by 5 by Mr Coad's rule, which I set down here as he wishes it kept. Tally to date 2,206.

units.author: camp_clerk_1894
units.text: Decr 5th. Still frost. Felled 33. Trewin would not go to the far lines after the lamps were lit, though only to fetch the saw he left. Mr Coad sent the boy instead, and the boy came back without it and would not say why. The saw fetched at first light, no harm to it. Roster 17 men. Let him that thinketh he standeth take heed.

units.title: Carrow Point light, keeper's log (E. Strake): extracts
units.author: carrow_keeper
units.text: Middle watch. 00:00 wind NW 3, vis. good, lamp trimmed. 01:30 wind NW 3, vis. good, clockwork wound. 02:15 lamp checked. Remarks: two walkers on the shore road below the light, going toward the village. Hailed from the gallery, did not answer. No vehicle. 03:45 wind backing W, vis. good. 04:00 relieved by assistant.

units.title: Gilliver Oral History Project (1976): tape 14, the window lamp
units.author: oral_history_1970s
units.text: Q: Did your mother keep a lamp in the window? A: Every night. Front window, the one facing the water. Q: What was it for? A: For the boats, she said. So the men coming in could see the village. [pause] Well. That's what she said to us. My father said it was so they'd know the house was awake. I never asked him who they were. You didn't.

units.title: Catalogue additions: storm ambiences
units.author: lowband_archivist
units.text: LB-2231. Wind, Carrow Point headland, storm conditions. Two omnis in blimps, 41 min. Gusts clipping at 34:10 and 36:02 (recordist's note). Dominant broadband wind noise, occasional halyard slap from the lighthouse flagpole. LB-2232. Rain on corrugated roof, Tollinby allotments, 22 min. Steady. Curator's note: the allotment shed has since blown over; the recordist sends regards to its owner.

units.title: Reminder: timesheet window (ref GLS-TS-0416)
units.author: grieve_payroll
units.text: This is an automated reminder. The site timesheet for contract KH-30 for the current pay week should be confirmed before the window closes at 23:59 in two days' time. Unconfirmed attendance will be carried forward at the recorded rate of $300 per worker per day. Do not reply to this message; this mailbox is not monitored.

units.author: sam
units.text: oh and I forgot, the Courier had another bit about your island today, something about it being halfway and nobody saying anything. Mum read it out to me down the phone in her newsreader voice. is it really fine out there? you'd say if it wasn't. you wouldn't, would you. anyway. the storm took our recycling bin lid and I found it two streets away. S x
